title: Investigate slow/red MCP indicator during sutra_status calls
description:
Josh reports sutra_status sometimes appears to hang — Claude Code's MCP indicator blinks red or stays red. Not a true hang, just slower than expected.

sutra/22 fixed the most likely cause: parse_workspace was async-without-awaits, blocking the tokio event loop during the sutra_status local fallback parse (when daemon unreachable) and during daemon HTTP handlers. All parse paths now use spawn_blocking.

If the symptom persists after sutra/22 lands, investigate:

1. **try_daemon_register HTTP timeout** — the TCP connect to the daemon could be slow if the daemon isn't running (depends on OS TCP timeout, not sutra). Consider adding a short connect_timeout (e.g. 500ms) so the local fallback kicks in faster.

2. **Daemon HTTP handler responsiveness** — even with spawn_blocking, if the daemon's axum thread pool is small and all threads are in spawn_blocking tasks, new HTTP requests queue. Check axum/hyper thread pool sizing.

3. **MCP keepalive timing** — Claude Code may have aggressive keepalive expectations. If sutra_status takes >N seconds even via the daemon path, the client may flag it. Measure actual latency of the daemon HTTP round-trip.

Next step: reproduce the red indicator after sutra/22 is deployed, then measure where the time goes (daemon connect, daemon handler, local fallback)."
